identity.title: Into the Mystic: the MUSE view of the ionized gas in the Mystic Mountains in Carina
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present optical integral field unit (IFU) observations of the Mystic Mountains, a dust pillar complex in the center of the Carina Nebula
combine it with recent ALMA observations of the cold molecular gas to estimate the remaining lifetime of the Mystic Mountains

question.value: What are the physical conditions (extinction, electron density and temperature, excitation) of the ionized gas in the Mystic Mountains, and what photoevaporation rate, remaining lifetime and protostar shielding time follow when combined with ALMA molecular gas masses?

evidence.quote: we measure the physical properties in the ionized gas including the electron density and temperature, excitation, and ionization.

We compute the photoevaporation rate of the Mystic Mountains and combine it with recent ALMA observations of the cold molecular gas to estimate the remaining lifetime of the Mystic Mountains and the corresponding shielding time for the embedded protostars.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2018.1.01001.S.

analysis_steps.goal: Reduce MUSE cubes with modified sky subtraction and continuum removal

method.value: MUSE recipes v.2.8.9 in EsoRex; modified five-step sky subtraction (muse_create_sky run twice, continuum zeroed, only OH and O2 telluric lines kept, muse_scipost); fourth-order polynomial continuum subtraction

evidence.quote: Data were reduced using the MUSE recipes v.2.8.9 (cite: weilbacher2012) in the EsoRex environment with standard calibrations.
To remove the continuum emission from the reduced data, we fit a fourth-order polynomial to a subset of pixels without strongly structured nebular emission and subtract this from the entire cube.

key_parameters.value: Wide-field mode, 1 arcmin x 1 arcmin field, R=2000-4000; three exposures per pointing with 90 deg rotation; long (780 s) and short (5 s) exposures

evidence.quote: At each pointing, three separate exposures were obtained with a 90$^{\circ}$ rotation between each to minimize detector artifacts.
each position was observed twice – once with short (5 s) exposures and once with long (780 s) exposures.

key_parameters.value: Long exposures used for most lines; short exposures for Halpha near HH 901 and HH 902 and for Halpha/Hbeta

evidence.quote: For the majority of the analysis in this paper, we use only the long exposures as these provide the best signal-to-noise for most lines.

assumptions.value: OH and O2 lines dominate telluric emission; all other telluric line fluxes set to zero

evidence.quote: we assume that OH and O$_2$ lines dominate the telluric emission; all other telluric line fluxes are set to zero.

method.value: Halpha/Hbeta ratio with PyNeb, CCM89 extinction curve, intrinsic ratio 2.86; extinction from short exposures applied to both short and long exposures

evidence.quote: The line-of-sight extinction was computed as a function of position using PyNeb (cite: luridiana2013; luridiana2015).
We use the extinction correction measured from the short exposures to correct the fluxes in both the short and long exposures.

We use PyNeb to compute these inter-related quantities simultaneously.

analysis_steps.goal: Map excitation and neutral carbon emission and trace ionization-front intensity profiles

method.value: He I 6678 / [S II] 6717,6731 ratio map for ionization degree; [C I] 8727 map; intensity profiles of lines of different excitation extracted along cuts across ionized interfaces

evidence.quote: We consider the ratio of lines with similar ionization potentials, He i $\lambda 6678$ Å / \[S ii\] $\lambda 6717,6731$ Å, to estimate the degree of ionization in the gas.
Finally, we extract the intensity profiles of emission lines of different excitation to trace the structure of the ionization fronts.

analysis_steps.goal: Compute local photoevaporation (mass-loss) rates at ionized interfaces

method.value: Cylinder illuminated from one side: Mdot ~ 2 pi r^2 m_H n_H v with n_H = 1.4 ne, v the ionized-gas sound speed (~10-12 km/s), r the radius of curvature of the best-matching circle at the pillar head

evidence.quote: we use the expression for a cylinder illuminated from one side from (cite: smith2004_finger)
We determine the radius of curvature from the radius of the circle that best matches the curvature at the pillar head.

evidence.quote: High electron densities, often in excess of 10$^3$ cm$^{-3}$, trace the heads of pillars and globules
Electron temperatures along the ionization front are typically near 10,000 K

evidence.quote: The HH 901 and HH 902 jets stand out as low-ionization structures
Only HH 901 shows extended

evidence.quote: We identify a new candidate jet located

evidence.quote: All seven continuum peaks are found immediately behind bright ionization fronts.

claims.hypothesis: Does the ionized gas in the pillars show compression traced by high electron densities?
claims.experiment: MUSE ne maps from [S II] ratio compared with ALMA C18O contours
claims.result: ne often exceeds 1e3 cm^-3 at pillar tips and ridges; C18O peaks lie behind high-ne ionization fronts except in the HH 901 pillar
claims.finding: High densities and small sizes of pillar heads suggest compression by external UV from Tr14

evidence.quote: High densities and small sizes of pillar heads suggest that they may have been compressed by external UV irradiation from Tr14.

claims.hypothesis: What is the remaining lifetime of the Mystic Mountains under photoevaporation?
claims.experiment: Cylinder mass-loss formula applied with MUSE ne and Te; combined with ALMA-derived molecular masses
claims.result: Whole complex 8 +/- 2 Myr; sub-regions ~1 to ~13 Myr; HH 901 tip >~2.5 Myr
claims.finding: The longest lifetimes are for the smallest structures independent of distance from the ionizing sources

evidence.quote: The longest lifetimes are for the smallest structures, independent of their relative distance from the ionizing sources.

claims.hypothesis: Does the data point to triggered star formation in the Mystic Mountains?
claims.experiment: Compare gas velocities from ALMA, jet bending, and pillar morphology with expectations for triggering
claims.result: Velocities and jet bending do not clearly show acceleration; HH 900, 901, 1066 globules give mixed evidence
claims.finding: Data are consistent with star formation being revealed as the cloud is evaporated; triggering is not required

evidence.quote: In-hand data are consistent with star formation being revealed as the cloud is evaporated.

claims.hypothesis: Can MUSE characterize the HH 901, 902, 1066 jets in different ionization states?
claims.experiment: Line ratio maps and P-V diagrams in Halpha, [S II], [O I], [C I], [Fe II]
claims.result: High-density low-ionization jets; marginally resolved velocities; extended [C I] only for HH 901
claims.finding: HH 901 [C I] likely traces dissociation of the molecular outflow in the HII region

evidence.quote: Only HH 901 shows extended [C i] emission, likely tracing the dissociation of the molecular outflow in the H ii region.

referee_caveats_inferred: Table 2 gives Mdot(HH901) = 2.0e-7 Msun/yr, the lowest value, but the text says HH 1066 has the lowest rate (~6e-7) and HH 901 is only ~2 times higher; the two are inconsistent
Uncertainties on the photoevaporation rate omit systematic error from the radius of curvature, geometry and the isothermal sound speed assumption
Lifetimes assume constant rate and that the molecular mass from a 6 arcsec ALMA map applies to sub-regions with large mass uncertainties (e.g. HH 901 3.31 +/- 2.64)
Table 1 exposure times (15 s) differ from the 5 s quoted in the text
Seeing-limited MUSE data may blend ionization-front structure at sub-arcsec scales
